To Thee the troops of Suras enter in, Some with joined palms in awe invoking Thee; Banded Maharshis, Siddhas, cry: "All hail"! Chanting Thy praises with resounding songs.
Rudras, Vasus, Sâdhyas and Adityas, Vishvas, the Ashvins, Maruts, Ushmapas, Gandharvas, Yakshas, Siddhas, Asuras, In wondering multitudes beholding Thee.
Thy mighty Form, with many mouths and eyes, Long armed, with thighs and feet innumerate, Vast-bosomed, set with many fearful teeth, The worlds see terror-struck, as also I.
Radiant, Thou touchest heaven, rainbow-hued, With opened mouths and shining vast-orbed eyes. My inmost self is quaking, having seen, My strength is withered, Vishnu, and my peace.
Like Time's destroying flames I see Thy teeth, Upstanding, spread within expanded jaws; Nought know I anywhere, no shelter find; Mercy, O God! re of all the worlds!
The sons of Dhṛitarâshtra, and with them The multitude of all these kings of earth, Bhîshma, and Drona, Sûta's royal son, And all the noblest warriors of our hosts,
Into Thy gaping mouths they hurrying rush, Tremendous-toothed and terrible to see; Some caught within the gaps between Thy teeth Are seen, their heads to powder crushed and ground.
As river-floods impetuously rush, Hurling their waters into ocean's lap, So fling themselves into Thy flaming mouths, In haste, these mighty men, these lords of earth.
As moths with quickened speed will headlong fly Into a flaming light, to fall destroyed, So also these, in haste precipitate, Enter within Thy mouths destroyed to fall.
On every side, all-swallowing, fiery-tongued, Thou lickest up mankind, devouring all; The glory filleth space: the universe Is burning, Vishnu, with Thy blazing rays.
Reveal Thy Self ; what awful Form art Thou? I worship Thee! Have mercy, God supreme! Thine inner Being I am fain to know; This Thy forth-streaming Life bewilders me.
Time am I, laying desolate the world, Made manifest on earth to slay mankind! Not one of all these warriors ranged for strife Escapeth death; thou shalt alone survive.
Therefore stand up! win for thyself renown, Conquer thy foes, enjoy the wealth filled realm, By Me they are already overcome, Be thou the outward cause, left-handed one.
Drona and Bhîshma and Jayadratha, Karna, and all the other warriors here, Are slain by Me. Destroy them fearlessly. Fight! thou shalt crush thy rivals in the field.
Having heard these words of Keshava, he who weareth a diadem, with joined palms, quaking and prostrating himself, spake again to Krishna, stammering with fear, casting down his face.
gita_besant.speaker: Sanjaya said

gita_besant.t: Hrishîkesha! in Thy magnificence Rightly the world rejoiceth, hymning Thee; The Râkshasas to every quarter fly In fear; the hosts of Siddhas prostrate fall.
How should they otherwise, O loftiest Self! First Cause! Brahmâ Himself less great than Thou. Infinite, God of Gods, home of all worlds, Unperishing, Sat, Asat, That supreme!
First of the Gods, most ancient Man Thou art. Supreme receptacle of all that lives; Knower and known, the dwelling-place on high; In Thy vast Form the universe is spread.
Thou art Vâyu and Yama, Agni, moon, Varuna, Father, Grandsire of all; Hail, hail to Thee! a thousand times all hail! Hail unto Thee! again, again all hail!
Prostrate in front of Thee, prostrate behind; Prostrate on every side to Thee, O All. In power boundless, measureless in strength, Thou holdest all: then Thou Thyself art All.
If, thinking Thee but friend, importunate, O Krishna! or O Yâdava! O friend! I cried, unknowing of Thy majesty, And careless in the fondness of my love;
If jesting I irreverence showed to Thee, At play, reposing, sitting or at meals, Alone, O sinless One, or with my friends, Forgive my error, O Thou boundless One.
There is none like to Thee. Who passeth Thee? Pre-eminent Thy power in all the worlds.
Therefore I fall before Thee; with my body I worship as it fitting; bless Thou me. As father with the son, as friend with friend, With the beloved as lover, bear with me.
I have seen that which none hath seen before, My heart is glad, yet faileth me for fear; Show me, O God, Thine other Form again— Mercy, O God of Gods, home of all worlds—
Diademed, mace and discus in Thy hand. Again I fain would see Thee as before; Put on again Thy four-armed shape, O Lord, O thousand-armed, of forms innumerate.
Radiant, all-penetrating, endless, first, That none except thyself hath ever seen.
Nor sacrifice, nor Vedas, alms, nor works, Nor sharp austerity, nor study deep, Can win the vision of this Form for man, Foremost of Kurus, thou alone hast seen.
Be not bewildered, be thou not afraid, Because thou hast beheld this awful Form; Cast fear away, and let thy heart rejoice; Behold again Mine own familiar shape.
Vâsudeva, having thus spoken to Arjuna, again manifested His own Form, and consoled the terrified one, the Mahâtman again assuming a gentle form.
gita_besant.speaker: Sanjaya said

gita_besant.t: Beholding again Thy gentle human Form, O Janârdana, I am now collected, and am restored to my own nature.
gita_besant.speaker: Arjuna said

gita_besant.t: This Form of Mine beholden by thee is very hard to see. Verily the Shining Ones ever long to behold this form.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Nor can I be seen as thou hast seen Me by the Vedas, nor by austerities, nor by alms, or by offerings;
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: But by devotion to Me alone I may thus be perceived, Arjuna, and known and seen in essence, and entered, O Parantapa.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He who doeth actions for Me, whose supreme good I am, My devotee, freed from attachment without hatred of any being, he cometh unto Me, O Pândava.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Those devotees who ever harmonised worship Thee, and those also who worship the Indestructible, the Unmanifested, whether of these is the more learned in yoga?
gita_besant.speaker: Arjuna said

gita_besant.t: They who with mind fixed on Me ever harmonised worship Me, with faith supreme endowed, these, in My opinion, are best in yoga.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: They who worship the Indestructible, the Ineffable, the unmanifested, Omnipresent, and Unthinkable, the Unchanging, Immutable, Eternal,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Restraining and subduing the senses, regarding everything equally, in the welfare of all rejoicing, these also come unto Me.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The difficulty of those whose minds are set on the Unmanifested is greater; for the path of the Unmanifested is hard for the embodied to reach.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Those verily who, renouncing all actions in Me and intent on Me, worship meditating on Me, with whole-hearted yoga,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: These I speedily lift up from the ocean of death and existence, O Pârtha, their minds being fixed on Me.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Place thy mind in me, into Me let thy Reason enter; then without doubt thou shalt abide in Me hereafter.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: And if thou art not able firmly to fix thy mind on Me, then by the yoga of practice seek to reach Me, O Dhananjaya.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: If also thou art not equal to constant practice, be intent on My service; performing actions for My sake, thou shalt attain perfection.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: If even to do this thou hast not strength, then, taking refuge in union with Me, renounce all fruit of action with the self controlled.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Better indeed is wisdom than constant-practice; than wisdom, meditation is better; than meditation, renunciation of the fruit of action; on renunciation follows peace.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He who beareth no ill-will to any being, friendly and compassionate, without attachment and egoism, balanced in pleasure and pain, and forgiving,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Ever content, harmonious, with the self-controlled, resolute, with mind and Reason dedicated to Me, he, My devotee, is dear to Me.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He from whom the world doth not shrink away, who doth not shrink away from the world, freed from the anxieties of joy, anger, and fear, he is dear to me.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He who wants nothing, is pure, expert, passionless, untroubled, renouncing every undertaking, he, My devotee, is dear to Me.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He who neither loveth nor hateth, nor grieveth, nor desireth, renouncing good and evil, full of devotion, he is dear to Me.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Alike to foe and friend, and also in fame and ignominy, alike in cold and heat, pleasures and pains, destitute of attachment,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Taking equally praise and reproach, silent, wholly content with what cometh, homeless, firm in mind, full of devotion, that man is dear to Me.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: They verily who partake of this life-giving wisdom as taught herein, endued with faith, I their supreme Object, devotees, they are surpassingly dear to Me.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Matter and Spirit, even the Field and the Knower of the Field, wisdom and that which ought to be known, these I fain would learn, O Keshava.
gita_besant.speaker: Arjuna said

gita_besant.t: This body, son of Kuntî, is called the Field; that which knoweth it is called the Knower of the Field by the Sages.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Understand Me as the Knower of the Field in all Fields, O Bhârata. Wisdom as to the Field and the Knower of the Field, that in My opinion is the wisdom.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: What that Field is and of what nature, how modified, and whence it is, and what He is and what His powers, hear that now briefly from Me.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Rishis have sung in manifold ways, in many various chants, and in decisive Brahma-sûtra verses full of reasonings.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The great Elements, Individuality , Reason , and also the unmanifested, the ten senses and the one, and the five pastures of the senses ;
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Desire, aversion, pleasure, pain, combination , intelligence, firmness; these, briefly described, constitute the Field and its modifications.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Humility, unpretentiousness, harmlessness, forgiveness, rectitude, service of the teacher, purity, steadfastness, self-control.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Dispassion towards the objects of the senses, and also absence of egoism, insight into the pain and evil of birth, death, old age and sickness,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Unattachment, absence of self-identification with son, wife or home, and constant balance of mind in wished-for and unwished-for events,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Unflinching devotion to Me by yoga, without other objects, resort to sequestered places, absence of enjoyment in the company of men,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Constancy in the wisdom of the Self, understanding of the object of essential wisdom; that is declared to be the Wisdom; all against it is ignorance.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: I will declare that which ought to be known, that which being known immortality is enjoyed—the beginningless supreme Eternal , called neither being nor non-being.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Everywhere That hath hands and feet, everywhere eyes, heads, and mouths; all-hearing, He dwelleth in the world, enveloping all,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Shining with all sense-faculties without any senses; unattached supporting everything and free from qualities enjoying qualities;
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Without and within all beings, immovable and also movable; by reason of His subtlety imperceptible; at hand and far away is That .
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Not divided amid beings, and yet seated distributively; that is to be known as the supporter of beings; He devours and He generates.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: That , the Light of all lights, is said to be beyond darkness; Wisdom, the Object of Wisdom, by Wisdom to be reached, seated in the hearts of all.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Thus the Field, Wisdom and the Object of Wisdom, have been briefly told. My devotee, thus knowing, enters into My Being.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Know thou that Matter and Spirit are both without beginning; and know thou also that modifications and qualities are all Matter -born.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Matter is called the cause of the generation of causes and effects; Spirit is called the cause of the enjoyment of pleasure and pain.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Spirit seated in Matter useth the qualities born of Matter ; attachment to the qualities is the cause of his births in good and evil wombs.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Supervisor and permitter, supporter, enjoyer, the great Lord, and also the supreme Self ; thus is styled in this body the supreme Spirit.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He who thus knoweth Spirit and Matter with its qualities, in whatsoever condition he may be, he shall not be born again.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Some by meditation behold the Self in the self by the Self ; others by the Sânkhya Yoga, and others by the Yoga of Action;
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Others also, ignorant of this, having heard of it from others, worship; and these also cross beyond death, adhering to what they had heard.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Whatsoever creature is born immobile or mobile, know thou, O best of the Bhâratas, that it is from the union between the Field and the Knower of the Field.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Seated equally in all beings, the supreme Lord, unperishing within the perishing—he who thus seeth, he seeth.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Seeing indeed everywhere the same Lord equally dwelling, he doth not destroy the Self , and thus treads the highest Path.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He who seeth that Matter verily performeth all actions, and that the Self is actionless, he seeth.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: When he perceiveth the diversified existence of beings as rooted in One, and spreading forth from it, then he reacheth the Eternal
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Being beginningless and without qualities , the imperishable supreme Self , though seated in the body, O Kaunteya, worketh not nor is affected.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: As the omnipresent ether is not affected, by reason of its subtlety, so seated everywhere in the body the Self is not affected.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: As the one sun illumineth the whole earth, so the Lord of the Field illumineth the whole Field, O Bhârata.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: They who by the eyes of Wisdom perceive this difference between the Field and the Knower of the Field, and the liberation of beings from Matter they go to the Supreme.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: I will again proclaim that supreme Wisdom, of all wisdom the best, which having known, all the Sages have gone hence to the supreme Perfection.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Having taken refuge in this Wisdom and being assimilated to My own nature, they are not re-born even in the emanation of a universe, nor are disquieted in the dissolution.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: My womb is the great Eternal ; in that I place the germ; thence cometh the birth of all beings, O Bhârata.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: In whatsoever wombs mortals are produced, O Kaunteya, the great Eternal is their womb, I their generating father.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Harmony, Motion, Inertia, such are the qualities , Matter -born; they bind fast in the body, O great-armed one, the indestructible dweller in the body.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Of these Harmony from its stainlessness, luminous and healthy, bindeth by the attachment to bliss and the attachment to wisdom, O sinless one.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Motion, the passion nature, know thou, is the source of attachment and thirst for life, O Kaunteya, that bindeth the dweller in the body by the attachment to action.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: But Inertia, know thou, born of unwisdom, is the deluder of all dwellers in the body; that bindeth by heedlessness, indolence and sloth, O Bharata .
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Harmony attacheth to bliss, Motion to action O Bharata . Inertia, verily, having shrouded wisdom, attacheth on the contrary to heedlessness.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Now Harmony prevaileth, having overpowered Motion and Inertia, O Bhârata; now Motion, having overpowered Harmony and Inertia; and now Inertia, having overpowered Harmony and Motion.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: When the wisdom-light streameth forth from all the gates of the body, then it may be known that Harmony is increasing.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Greed, outgoing energy, undertaking of actions, restlessness, desire—these are born of the increase of Motion, O best of the Bhâratas.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Darkness, stagnation and heedlessness and also delusion—these are born of the increase of Inertia, O joy of the Kurus.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: If Harmony verily prevaileth when the embodied goeth to dissolution, then he goeth forth to the spotless worlds of the great Sages.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Having gone to dissolution in Motion, he is born among those attached to action; if dissolved in Inertia, he is born in the wombs of the senseless.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: It is said the fruit of a good action is harmonious and spotless; verily the fruit of Motion is pain, and the fruit of Inertia unwisdom
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: From Harmony wisdom is born, and also greed from Motion; heedlessness and delusion are of Inertia and also unwisdom.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: They rise upwards who are settled in Harmony; the Active dwell in the mid-most place: the Inert go downwards, enveloped in the vilest
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: When the Seer perceiveth no agent other than the qualities , and knoweth That which is higher than the qualities, he entereth into My Nature.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: When the dweller in the body hath crossed over these three qualities, whence all bodies have been produced, liberated from birth, death, old age and sorrow, he drinketh the nectar of immortality .
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: What are the marks of him who hath crossed over the three qualities , O Lord? How acteth he, and how doth he go beyond these three qualities ?
gita_besant.speaker: Arjuna said

gita_besant.t: He, O Pândava, who hateth not radiance, nor outgoing energy, nor even delusion, when present, nor longeth after them, absent;
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He who, seated as a neutral, is unshaken by the qualities ; who, saying, "The qualities revolve," standeth apart immovable.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Balanced in pleasure and pain, self-reliant, to whom a lump of earth, a rock and gold are alike, the same to loved and unloved, firm, the same in censure and in praise,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The same in honour and ignominy, the same to friend and foe, abandoning all undertakings—he is said to have crossed over the qualities.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: And he who serveth Me exclusively by the Yoga of devotion, he, crossing beyond the qualities, he is fit to become the Eternal .
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: For I am the abode of the Eternal , and of the indestructible nectar of immortality, of immemorial righteousness, and of unending bliss.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: With roots above, branches below, the Asvattha is said to be indestructible; the leaves of it are hymns; he who knoweth it is a Veda-knower.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Downwards and upwards spread the branches of it, nourished by the qualities ; the objects of the senses its buds; and its roots grow downwards, the bonds of action in the world of men.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Nor here may be acquired knowledge of its form, nor its end, nor its origin, nor its rooting-place; this strongly rooted Asvattha having been cut down by the unswerving weapon of non-attachment,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: That path beyond may be sought, treading which there is no return. I go indeed to that Primal Man , whence the ancient energy forth-streamed.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Without pride and delusion, victorious over the vice of attachment, dwelling constantly in the Self , desire pacified, liberated from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain, they tread, undeluded, that indestructible path.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Nor doth the sun lighten there, nor moon, nor fire; having gone thither they return not; that is My supreme abode.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: A portion of Mine own Self, transformed in the world of life into an immortal Spirit, draweth round itself the senses of which the mind is the sixth, veiled in matter .
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: When the Lord acquireth a body and when He abandoneth it, He seizeth these and goeth with them, as the wind takes fragrances from their retreats
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Enshrined in the ear, the eye, the touch, the taste and the smell, and in the mind also, He enjoyeth the objects of the senses
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The deluded do not perceive (Him) when He departeth or stayeth or enjoyeth, swayed by the qualities ; the wisdom-eyed perceive.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Yogîs also, struggling, perceive Him, established in the Self ; but though struggling, the unintelligent perceive Him not, their selves untrained.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: That splendour issuing from the sun that enlighteneth the whole world, that which is in the moon and in fire, that splendour know as from Me.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Permeating the soil, I support beings by my vital energy, and having become the delicious Soma I nourish all plants.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: I, having become the Fire of Life , take possession of the bodies of breathing things, and united with the life-breaths , I digest the four kinds of food.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: And I am seated in the hearts of all, and from Me memory and wisdom and their absence. And that which is to be known in all the Vedas am I; and I indeed the Veda-knower and the author of the Vedanta.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: There are two Energies in this world, the destructible and the indestructible; the destructible is all beings, the unchanging is called the indestructible.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The highest Energy is verily Another, declared as the Supreme Self , He who, pervading all, sustaineth the three worlds, the indestructible Lord.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Since I excel the destructible, and am more excellent also than the indestructible, in the world and in the Veda I am proclaimed the Supreme Spirit.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He who undeluded knoweth Me thus as the Supreme Spirit , he, all-knowing, worshippeth Me with his whole being, O Bhârata.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Thus by Me this most secret teaching hath been told O sinless one. This known, he hath become illuminated and hath finished his work, O Bhârata.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Fearlessness, cleanness of life, steadfastness in the Yoga of wisdom, almsgiving, self-restraint and sacrifice and study of the Scriptures, austerity and straightforwardness,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Harmlessness, truth, absence of wrath, renunciation, peacefulness, absence of crookedness, compassion to living beings, uncovetousness, mildness, modesty, absence of fickleness,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Vigour, forgiveness, fortitude, purity, absence of envy and pride—these are his who is born with the divine properties, O Bhârata.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Hypocrisy, arrogance and conceit, wrath and also harshness and unwisdom are his who is born, O Pârtha, with demoniacal properties.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The divine properties are deemed to be for liberation, the demoniacal for bondage. Grieve not, thou art born with divine properties, O Pândava.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Twofold is the animal creation in this world, the divine and the demoniacal: the divine hath been described at length: hear from Me, O Pârtha, the demoniacal.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Demoniacal men know neither right energy nor right abstinence; nor purity, nor even propriety, nor truth is in them.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: "The universe is without truth, without basis," they say, "without a God ; brought about by mutual union, and caused by lust and nothing else."
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Holding this view, these ruined selves of small understanding , of fierce deeds, come forth as enemies for the destruction of the world.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Surrendering themselves to insatiable desires, possessed with vanity, conceit and arrogance, holding evil ideas through delusion, they engage in action with impure resolves.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Giving themselves over to unmeasured thought whose end is death, regarding the gratification of desires as the highest, feeling sure that this is all,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Held in bondage by a hundred ties of expectation, given over to lust and anger, they strive to obtain by unlawful means hoards of wealth for sensual enjoyments.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: "This to-day by me hath been won, that purpose I shall gain; this wealth is mine already, and also this shall be mine in future.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: "I have slain this enemy, and others also I shall slay. I am the Lord, I am the enjoyer, I am perfect, powerful, happy;
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: "I am wealthy, well-born; what other is there that is like unto me? I will sacrifice, I will give alms, I will rejoice." Thus deluded by unwisdom,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Bewildered by numerous thoughts, enmeshed in the web of delusion, addicted to the gratification of desire, they fall downwards into a foul hell.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Self-glorifying, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform lip-sacrifices for ostentation, contrary to scriptural ordinance.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Given over to egoism, power, insolence, lust and wrath, these malicious ones hate Me in the bodies of others and in their own.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: These haters, evil, pitiless, vilest among men in the world, I ever throw down into demoniacal wombs.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Cast into demoniacal wombs, deluded birth after birth, attaining not to Me, O Kaunteya, they sink into the lowest depths.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Triple is the gate of this hell, destructive of the self—lust, wrath, and greed; therefore let man renounce these three.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: A man liberated from these three gates of darkness, O son of Kunti, accomplisheth his own welfare, and thus reacheth the highest goal.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He who, having cast aside the ordinances of the Scriptures, followeth the promptings of desire, attaineth not to perfection, nor happiness, nor the highest goal.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Therefore let the Scriptures be thy authority, in determining what ought to be done, or what ought not to be done. Knowing what hath been declared by the ordinances of the Scriptures, thou oughtest to work in this world.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Those that sacrifice full of faith, but casting aside the ordinances of the Scriptures, what is verily their condition, O Krishna? Is it one of Purity, Passion, or Darkness ?
gita_besant.speaker: Arjuna said

gita_besant.t: Threefold is by nature the inborn faith of the embodied—pure, passionate, and dark. Hear thou of these.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The faith of each is shaped to his own nature, O Bhârata. The man consists of his faith ; that which his faith is, he is even that.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Pure men worship the Gods; the passionate the gnomes and giants ; the others, the dark folk, worship ghosts and troops of nature-spirits .
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The men who perform severe austerities, unenjoined by the Scriptures, wedded to vanity and egoism, impelled by the force of their desires and passions,
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Unintelligent, tormenting the aggregated elements forming the body, and Me also, seated in the inner body, know these demoniacal in their resolves.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The food also which is dear to each is threefold, as also sacrifice, austerity and almsgiving. Hear thou the distinction of these.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The foods that augment vitality, energy, vigour, health, joy and cheerfulness, delicious, bland, substantial and agreeable, are dear to the pure.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The passionate desire foods that are bitter, sour, saline, over-hot, pungent, dry and burning and which produce pain, grief and sickness.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: That which is stale and flat, putrid and corrupt, leavings also and unclean, is the food dear to the dark.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for fruit, as enjoined by the ordinances, under the firm belief that sacrifice is a duty, that is pure.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The sacrifice offered with a view verily to fruit, and also indeed for self-glorification, O best of the Bhâratas; know thou that to be of passion.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The sacrifice contrary to the ordinances, without distributing food, devoid of words of power and without gifts , empty of faith, is said to be of darkness.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Worship given to the Gods, to the twice-born, to the teachers and to the wise, purity, straightforwardness, continence and harmlessness, are called the austerity of the body.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Speech causing no annoyance, truthful, pleasant and beneficial, the practice of the study of the Scriptures, are called the austerity of speech.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Mental happiness, equilibrium, silence, self-control, purity of nature—these are called the austerity of the mind .
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: This threefold austerity, performed by men with the utmost faith, without desire for fruit, harmonised, is said to be pure.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The austerity which is practised with the object of gaining respect, honour and worship, and for ostentation, is said to be of passion, unstable and fleeting.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: That austerity done under a deluded understanding, with self-torture, or with the object of destroying another, that is declared of darkness.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: That alms given to one who does nothing in return, believing that a gift ought to be made in a fit place and time to a worthy person, that alms is accounted pure.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: That given with a view to receiving in return, or looking for fruit again, or grudgingly, that alms is accounted of passion.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: That alms given at unfit place and time, and to unworthy persons, disrespectfully and contemptuously, that is declared of darkness.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: " Aum Tat Sat ," this has been considered to be the threefold designation of the Eternal . By that were ordained of old Brâhmanas, Vedas and sacrifices.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Therefore with the pronunciation of " Aum " the acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity as laid down in the ordinances are always commenced by the knowers of the Eternal .
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: With the pronunciation of " Tat " and without aiming at fruit are performed the various acts of sacrifice, austerity and gift, by those desiring liberation.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: " Sat " is used in the sense of reality and goodness; likewise, O Pârtha, the word " Sat " is used in the sense of a good work.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity and gift is also called " Sat ", and action for the sake of the Supreme is also named " Sat ."
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Whatsoever is wrought without faith, oblation, gift, austerity, or other deed, "Asat" it is called, O Pârtha; it is nought, here or hereafter.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: I desire, O mighty-armed, to know severally the essence of renunciation, O Hrishîkesha, and of relinquishment , O Keshinishûdana .
gita_besant.speaker: Arjuna said

gita_besant.t: Sages have known as renunciation the renouncing of works with desire; the relinquishing of the fruit of all actions is called relinquishment by the wise.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: "Action should be relinquished as an evil," declare some thoughtful men; "acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be relinquished," say others.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Hear my conclusions as to that relinquishment, O best of the Bhâratas; since relinquishment, O tiger of men, has been explained as threefold.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Acts of sacrifice, gift and austerity should not be relinquished, but should be performed; sacrifice, gift and also austerity are the purifiers of the intelligent.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: But even these actions should be done leaving aside attachment and fruit, O Pârtha; that is my certain and best belief.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Verily renunciation of actions that are prescribed is not proper; the relinquishment thereof from delusion is said to be of darkness.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He who relinquisheth an action from fear of physical suffering, saying "Painful," thus performing a passionate relinquishment, obtaineth not the fruit of relinquishment.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He who performeth a prescribed action, saying, "it ought to be done," O Arjuna, relinquishing attachment and also fruit, that relinquishment is regarded as pure.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The relinquisher pervaded by purity, intelligent and with doubts cut away, hateth not unpleasurable action nor is attached to pleasurable.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Nor indeed can embodied beings completely relinquish action; verily he who relinquisheth the fruit of action, he is said to be a relinquisher.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Good, evil and mixed—threefold is the fruit of action hereafter for the non-relinquisher; but there is none ever for the renouncer.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: These five causes, O mighty-armed, learn of Me as declared in the Sâñkhya system for the accomplishment of all actions:
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The body, the actor, the various organs, the diverse kinds of energies, and the presiding deities also, the fifth.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Whatever action a man performeth by his body, speech and mind, whether right or the reverse, these five are the cause thereof.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: That being so, he verily who—owing to untrained Reason —looketh on his Self , which is isolated, as the actor, he of perverted intelligence, seeth not.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: He who is free from the egoistic notion, whose Reason is not affected, though he slay these peoples, he slayeth not, nor is bound.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Knowledge, the knowable and the knower, the threefold impulse to action; the organ, the action, the actor, the threefold constituents of action.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Knowledge, action and actor in the category of qualities are also said to be severally threefold, from the difference of qualities ; hear thou duly these also.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: That by which one indestructible Being is seen in all beings, inseparate in the separated, know thou that knowledge as pure.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: But that knowledge which regardeth the several manifold existences in all beings as separate, that knowledge know thou as of passion;
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: While that which clingeth to each one thing as if it were the whole, without reason, without grasping the reality, narrow, that is declared to be dark.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: An action which is ordained, done by one undesirous of fruit, devoid of attachment, without love or hate, that is called pure.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: But that action that is done by one longing for desires, or again with egoism, or with much effort, that is declared to be passionate.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The action undertaken from delusion, without regard to capacity and consequences—loss and injury to others—that is declared to be dark.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Liberated from attachment, not egoistic, endued with firmness and confidence, unchanged by success or failure, that actor is called pure.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Impassioned, desiring to obtain the fruit of actions, greedy, harmful, impure, moved by joy and sorrow, such an actor is pronounced passionate.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: Discordant, vulgar, stubborn, cheating, malicious, indolent, despairful, procrastinating, that actor is called dark.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The division of Reason and of firmness also, threefold according to the qualities , hear thou related, unreservedly and severally, O Dhananjaya.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: That which knoweth energy and abstinence, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation, that Reason is pure, O Pârtha.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: That by which one understandeth away Right and Wrong and also what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, that Reason, O Pârtha, is passionate.
gita_besant.speaker: The Blessed Lord said

gita_besant.t: The unwavering firmness by which, through Yoga, one restraineth the activity of the mind , of the life breaths and of the sense-organs, that firmness, O Pârtha, is pure.
But the firmness, O Arjuna, by which, from attachment desirous of fruit, one holdeth fast duty , desire and wealth, that firmness, O Pârtha, is passionate.
That by which one from stupidity doth not abandon sleep, fear, grief, despair, and also vanity, that firmness, O Pârtha, is dark.
And now the threefold kinds of pleasure hear thou from Me, O bull of the Bhâratas. That in which one by practice rejoiceth, and which putteth an end to pain;
Which at first is as venom but in the end is as nectar; that pleasure is said to be pure, born of the blissful knowledge of the Self .
That which from the union of the senses with their objects at first is as nectar, but in the end is like venom, that pleasure is accounted passionate.
That pleasure which both at first and afterwards is delusive of the self, arising from sleep, indolence and heedlessness, that is declared dark.
There is not an entity, either on the earth or again in heaven among the Shining Ones, that is liberated from these three qualities, born of Matter .
Of Brâhmanas, Kshattriyas, Vaishyas and Shûdras, O Parantapa, the duties have been distributed, according to the qualities born of their own natures.
Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness and also uprightness, wisdom, knowledge, belief in God, are the Brâhmana duty , born of his own nature.
Prowess, splendour, firmness, dexterity, and also not flying from battle, generosity, the nature of a ruler, are the Kshattriya duty , born of his own nature.
Ploughing, protection of kine, and trade are the Vaishya duty , born of his own nature. Action of the nature of service is the Shûdra duty, born of his own nature.
Man reacheth perfection by each being intent on his own duty . Listen thou how perfection is won by him who is intent on his own duty .
He from whom is the emanation of beings, by Whom all This is pervaded, by worshipping Him in his own duty a man winneth perfection.
Better is one's own duty though destitute of merits than the well-executed duty of another. He who doeth the duty laid down by his own nature incurreth not sin.
Congenital duty , O son of Kunti, though defective, ought not to be abandoned. All undertakings indeed are clouded by defects as fire by smoke.
He whose Reason is everywhere unattached, the self-subdued, dead to desires, he goeth by renunciation to the supreme perfection of freedom from obligation.
How he who hath attained perfection obtaineth the Eternal , that highest state of wisdom, learn thou from Me only succinctly, O Kaunteya.
United to this Reason, purified, controlling the self by firmness, having abandoned sound and the other objects of the senses, having laid aside passion and malice,
Dwelling in solitude, abstemious, speech, body and mind subdued, constantly fixed in meditation and yoga , taking refuge in dispassion,
Having cast aside egoism, violence, arrogance, desire, wrath, covetousness, selfless and peaceful—he is fit to become the Eternal .
Becoming the Eternal , serene in the Self , he neither grieveth nor desireth; the same to all beings, he obtaineth supreme devotion unto Me.
By devotion he knoweth Me in essence, who and what I am; having thus known Me in essence he forthwith entereth into the Supreme.
Though ever performing all actions, taking refuge in Me, by My grace he obtaineth the eternal indestructible abode.
Renouncing mentally all works in Me, intent on Me, resorting to the yoga of discrimination , have thy thought ever on Me.
Thinking on Me, thou shalt overcome all obstacles by My grace: but if from egoism thou wilt not listen, thou shalt be destroyed utterly.
Entrenched in egoism, thou thinkest, "I will not fight;" to no purpose thy determination; nature will constrain thee.
O son of Kuntî, bound by thine own duty born of thine own nature, that which from delusion thou desirest not to do, even that helplessly thou shalt perform.
The Lord dwelleth in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, by His illusive Power causing all beings to revolve, as though mounted on a potter's wheel.
Flee unto Him for shelter with all thy being, O Bhârata; by His grace thou shalt obtain supreme peace, the everlasting dwelling-place.
Thus hath wisdom, more secret than secrecy itself, been declared unto thee by Me; having reflected on it fully, then act thou as thou listest.
Listen thou again to My supreme word, most secret of all; beloved art thou of Me, and steadfast of heart, therefore will I speak for thy benefit.
Merge thy mind in Me, be my devotee, sacrifice to Me, prostrate thyself before Me, thou shalt come even to Me. I pledge thee My troth; thou art dear to Me.
Abandoning all duties come unto Me alone for shelter; sorrow not, I will liberate thee from all sins.
Never is this to be spoken by thee to anyone who is without asceticism, nor without devotion, nor to one who desireth not to listen, nor yet to him who speaketh evil of Me.
He who shall declare this supreme secret among My devotees, having shown the highest devotion for Me, without doubt he shall come to Me.
Nor is there any among men who performeth dearer service to Me than he, nor any other shall be more beloved by Me on earth than he.
And he who shall study this sacred dialogue of ours, by him I shall be worshipped with the sacrifice of wisdom. Such is My mind.
The man also who, full of faith, merely heareth it unreviling, even he, freed from evil, obtaineth the radiant worlds of the righteous.
Hath this been heard, O son of Prithâ, with one-pointed mind? Has thy delusion, caused by unwisdom, been destroyed, O Dhananjaya?
Destroyed is my delusion. I have gained knowledge through Thy grace, O Immutable one. I am firm, my doubts have fled away. I will do according to Thy word.
gita_besant.speaker: Arjuna said

gita_besant.t: I heard this marvellous dialogue of Vâsudeva, and of the great-souled Partha, causing my hair to stand on end.
gita_besant.speaker: Sanjaya said

gita_besant.t: By the favour of Vyâsa I listened to this secret and supreme yoga from the Lord of Yoga, Krishna Himself, speaking before mine eyes.
gita_besant.speaker: Sanjaya said

gita_besant.t: O King, remembering, remembering this marvellous and holy dialogue between Keshava and Arjuna, I rejoice again and again.
gita_besant.speaker: Sanjaya said

gita_besant.t: Remembering, remembering, also that most marvellous form of Hari, great is my wonder, O King. I rejoice, again and again.
gita_besant.speaker: Sanjaya said

gita_besant.t: Wherever is Krishna, Yoga's Lord, wherever is Pârtha, the archer, assured are there prosperity, victory and happiness. So I think.
gita_besant.speaker: Sanjaya said
